I am 58 years old and I have farmed these fields in Quzhou for 40 years. I finished high school, so I can read fertilizer labels and calculate nutrient rates myself, and I pay attention to what the agricultural extension station puts on WeChat, but I still trust what I see with my own eyes more than anything on paper. My 7.5 mu are split into two parts: 5 mu in wheat-maize rotation and 2.5 mu for kohlrabi as a cash crop. It is just me and my wife at home now — our son works in a factory in Handan and sends money back, but I do not touch that for farming. I pay for all inputs from crop sales.

For the wheat: I sowed an improved Jimai variety last October after rotary tillage. I put down 50 kg per mu of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer as base. Now at green-up, I will spread 20 kg per mu of urea, and probably another 5 kg per mu at the jointing stage if the plants look yellow. That comes to about 16 kg of nitrogen, 7 kg of phosphorus, and 7 kg of potassium per mu. The soil in my field is loam with medium potassium, but I would rather have a little extra than see the leaves yellow at heading — a 50-yuan bag of fertilizer is cheap insurance against losing 100 kg of grain. I will irrigate four times total: overwinter watering was already done, and this spring I will water at green-up, jointing, and grain filling. Two sprays: one herbicide for catchweed grass and one fungicide for stripe rust. I expect 520 kg per mu if the weather holds.

For maize: Right after wheat harvest in early June, I will no-till drill hybrid Zhengdan 958 on the same 5 mu. No-till saves me three days of labor and I do not lose moisture at sowing time. I will band 40 kg per mu of 15-15-15 in the seed furrow, then side-dress 25 kg per mu of urea at the big trumpet stage. That is roughly 18 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. Three irrigations: seedling establishment, jointing, and filling. Two pesticide applications, mainly for armyworm and weed control. I am targeting 600 kg per mu. I will hire two day-laborers at 150 yuan per day each for the planting rush because that ten-day window cannot be missed.

For kohlrabi: I plant 2.5 mu of improved kohlrabi as a spring crop on the plot closest to the well. This land gets rotary tilled and 50 kg per mu of 15-15-15 base fertilizer. After the plants rosette, I side-dress 30 kg per mu of urea and 15 kg per mu of potassium chloride because kohlrabi is a heavy potassium feeder and the bulbs will not swell without it. Total nutrients are about 21 kg nitrogen, 7.5 kg phosphorus, and 16.5 kg potassium per mu. Four irrigations to keep the soil moist — woody kohlrabi gets rejected by the vegetable broker. Three sprays for diamondback moth and cabbage worm. I should get 2,500 kg per mu, sold to the broker who drives to the village.

I watch my costs carefully. A 50 kg bag of urea is about 120 yuan now, compound is around 150 yuan. For the whole farm I am looking at about 4,500 yuan in chemical fertilizer, which is a lot of money for two people, but if I cut back and the yield drops 10 percent, I lose twice that much in grain and vegetable sales. My neighbor tried cutting nitrogen on wheat last year and his yield fell to 400 kg per mu — I am not making that mistake. I do what worked before, maybe adjust 5 to 10 percent based on seed price and spring rainfall, but no big experiments. The well water is reliable so I irrigate when the crops need it.
